text: {"en": ["Among the methods [the Sages] of blessed memory employed in their teaching, knowledge of which will remove the veil of many doubts from before our eyes,", "there is one we must likewise consider, which the Kuzari and the Riaz also touched upon in their remarks cited above.", "It is that our Sages, in many of their pure sayings, made use of exaggeration and hyperbole,", "after the manner of people who multiply lofty speech, whether about matters or about numerical sums, stating neither the actual truth nor anything close to it, but rather to indicate that something is greater than we would believe it to be.", "This accords with their own remark in chapter Gid ha-Nasheh, \"The Sages spoke in exaggerated language\" [b. Hullin 90b], and in several places they said, \"It is stated as hyperbole.\"", "With regard to numbers, see their sayings which we cited in chapter 13 about the number of Jews in Alexandria of Egypt and in Betar: \"six hundred thousand myriads by six hundred thousand myriads,\" and some say \"eighty thousand myriads\";", "and in chapter Ha-Memuneh: \"R. Eleazar ben Harsom owned a thousand towns, and corresponding to them ships at sea\" [b. Yoma 35b];", "and in chapter Elu Terefot: \"thirteen scrolls\" (or \"camels,\" according to Rashi's reading) \"of doubtful terefot\";", "and in chapter Tamid Nishhat: \"Between 'Azel' and 'Azel' [they] loaded four hundred camels of exegesis\" [b. Pesahim 62b].", "And in the first chapter of Eruvin it appears explicitly that \"one hundred and upward\" is not meant precisely,", "when they say: \"Granted, according to Bar Kappara, 'a hundred' is hyperbole; but according to Rav Judah, whence do we derive it?\"", "In particular, the sum of eighty and eighty thousand you will find frequently used as hyperbole in the Yerushalmi, Ta'anit, chapter Bi-Sheloshah Perakim.", "Likewise the number sixty is frequent in the Babylonian Gemara: besides the five \"one-sixtieth\" sayings of chapter Ha-Ro'eh [b. Berakhot 57b], and similar ones in chapter Mi she-Hayah and others in chapter Ein Bein, and the like,", "see in chapter Ha-Sokher, concerning the sufferings of R. Eleazar: \"sixty felt sheets,\" \"sixty kinds of bloodletting\" [b. Bava Metzia 84b], and much more there;", "and in chapter Ha-Hovel: \"sixty runners ran,\" on which the Tosafot wrote explicitly: \"This is the Gemara's manner, as in Elu Terefot, 'sixty kinds of iron,' etc.\"", "There too, on \"sixty afflictions come upon,\" Rashi wrote: \"It is merely a figure of speech people use, and not meant precisely.\"", "*) And more than all the sums mentioned, you will find the number three hundred customary with them, of blessed memory, as we shall further mention in this chapter.", "So too in matters of intent: when, for example, they wished to distance a person with all their might from a transgression, they exaggerated in describing its harms,", "as when they said in chapter Yesh be-Arakhin that one who speaks slander magnifies his sins to equal the three [transgressions] concerning which they said \"let him be killed rather than transgress\" [b. Arakhin 15b];", "and in Nedarim: \"R. Akiva said: Whoever does not visit the sick is as though he shed blood\" [b. Nedarim 40a];", "and in chapter Ha-Oreg: \"One who tears his garments in his anger, let him be in your eyes like an idolater\" [b. Shabbat 105b],", "just as the sage Bar Sheshet [Ribash] in Responsum 171 cited these three sayings as proof of what he wrote, as follows:", "\"It is the way of the Sages to exaggerate in magnifying sins so that a person will guard himself from stumbling in them.\"", "Likewise you will find Maimonides, in his commentary on the Mishnah of Arba Mitot, saying of certain transgressions: \"They spoke at length to threaten and frighten, to the point that concerning some of them they caused alarm and said that there is no repentance for them,\"", "while the first chapter of Rosh ha-Shanah confirms their beneficial general principle: \"There is nothing that stands before it [repentance].\"", "Add to this that you can interpret their intent in \"he has no repentance\"", "[to mean] that the nature of that sin is such that its repentance is, for certain reasons, remote or impossible, as in the many [cases] that the Rambam, of blessed memory, mentioned in Hilkhot Teshuvah, chapter 4.", "And likewise, conversely, when they wished to urge and encourage some praiseworthy act, they went beyond measure,", "as when they said in the first chapter of Bava Batra: \"Greater is one who gives charity in secret than Moses our teacher\" [b. Bava Batra 9b];", "and in Ketubbot, chapter 6: \"Whoever averts his eyes from charity is as though he worships idols\" [b. Ketubbot 68a];", "and in the first chapter of Megillah: \"Whoever reports a saying in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world\" [b. Megillah 15a],", "though they brought this closer to reason by saying, \"Thus you have learned a practical lesson\": how through this very quality the great deliverance already came to Israel,", "and so anyone who holds to it may bring about the like. And there are many such in various matters.", "For this (I mean exaggeration in speech) is in truth the wisdom of the prudent and a fitting way to instill our intention into the hearer's heart,", "just as you know their saying, also in chapter Gid ha-Nasheh, that it is customary in Holy Scripture,", "which is without doubt a lamp and light to every master of language and eloquence.", "The rhetoricians, too, truly praised it and adhered to it, as you will find in their chief, Tullio [Cicero], in the fourth [book] of the Topica,", "and Quintilian in the eighth [book] of his Oratory, chapter 6, from whom the Jewish rhetorician, author of Sefer Nofet Tzufim, drew, in Gate 4, chapter 43. ⚠", "And although it is not our intention in this work to expound the methods of the Gemara and the particulars of the Midrashim,", "I have thought it worthwhile to touch upon this channel, which is truly a great principle for bringing such statements of theirs close to reason,", "in order to resolve a particular difficulty apparent in an account our Sages related, from which you may also infer to every similar case,", "since it is the accounts narrated by them that we are now discussing, as we have set forth.", "For in our Gemara, first chapter of Yoma: \"R. Yohanan said: What is meant by 'but the years of the wicked shall be shortened' [Prov 10:27]? This is the Second Temple, which stood four hundred and twenty years, and more than three hundred high priests served in it\" [b. Yoma 9a].", "Yet in the Yerushalmi, Yoma, first chapter, they said: \"In the Second Temple, where the high priests would obtain [the office] for money—and some say they would kill one another by sorcery—", "eighty high priests served in it; some say eighty-one, some say eighty-two, some say eighty-three, some say eighty-four, some say eighty-five\" [y. Yoma 1:1].", "Is this not a great contradiction between the two Gemaras? It is especially difficult since R. Yohanan himself, author of the Babylonian saying, is the one who compiled the Yerushalmi, and he should at least have said, \"and some say more than three hundred.\"", "However, by the remark we have set forth, it seems possible to resolve [it]: the Babylonian saying is not meant precisely but by way of hyperbole,", "while the Yerushalmi's statement is the exact figure in their opinion. This is also implied by its saying all those \"some say,\" each one being precise about his fellow's reckoning;", "and you will find it so also in Vayikra Rabbah and in Sifrei, as below. And do not look to the Babylonian's descending into actual counting when it says, \"Subtract from them the forty years of Simeon the Just, the eighty of Yohanan the High Priest,\" etc.,", "\"from then on, go and reckon that none of them completed his year\";", "for all is fitted to its aforementioned hyperbole, in the manner we wrote concerning Titus in chapter 16,", "and in the manner the Master, the Guide [Maimonides], wrote in his introduction regarding the parable \"For at the window of my house\" [Prov 7:6], to which many details were added that bear no relation to the thing signified but only serve to beautify the parable and give it the completeness appropriate to the intention of those who devised it.", "So too you will understand their saying we cited above, \"and some say eighty thousand myriads\";", "for though it appears to be a precise correction of the preceding sum, both are hyperboles that never were and never existed.", "Among the Christians, too, you will find the learned Ficino, in his commentary on Plato's Symposium (Convivio), Speech 4, chapter 2, who said, also in the name of their chief sage, exactly what the Master, the Guide, said as we mentioned. ⚠", "Now this sum of three hundred mentioned is very customary with our Sages by way of hyperbole,", "as when they said in the first chapter of Megillah: \"The great city of Rome is three hundred parasangs by three hundred parasangs\" [b. Megillah 6b];", "and in chapter Arba Mitot, also in Avot de-Rabbi Natan chapter 24: \"R. Eliezer used to teach three hundred laws concerning the bright white spot, and corresponding to them concerning the planting of cucumbers\";", "and in chapter Ehad Dinei: \"R. Meir had three hundred fox fables\" [b. Sanhedrin 38b]; and in chapter Yesh be-Korbanot: \"Three hundred laws were forgotten during the days of mourning for Moses\" [b. Temurah 16a];", "and in chapter Ein Dorshin and chapter Helek: \"three hundred laws concerning the tower flying in the air\";", "and in the first chapter of Yevamot: \"three hundred answers [given] to Jonathan concerning the co-wife of the daughter\"; and in chapter Makom she-Nahagu: \"Yohanan ben Narbai would eat three hundred calves and drink three hundred jugs of wine\" [b. Pesahim 57a];", "and in chapter Tamid Nishhat: \"Beruriah, the wife of R. Meir, learned three hundred teachings a day from the Book of Genealogies\" [b. Pesahim 62b];", "and in the first chapter of Shabbat: \"These are among the laws they stated in the upper chamber of Hananiah ben Hezekiah ben Garon\"—[he brought up] three hundred jugs of oil, sat in the upper chamber and expounded [b. Shabbat 13b]; ⚠", "and in Bekhorot, chapter Ma'aser: \"The egg of the bar yokhni fell and flooded sixty towns and broke three hundred cedars\" [b. Bekhorot 57b];", "and in Midrash Eikhah on \"[How the Lord] has covered\": \"Simeon used to bring out three hundred jugs of spiced wine\";", "and on the verse \"The Lord is righteous\" [Lam 1:18]: \"They shot three hundred arrows at Josiah\";", "and they said the like also concerning R. Judah ben Bava in Sanhedrin and in tractate Avodah Zarah, chapter 1;", "and in Tanhuma, end of Vayakhel: \"Three hundred priests would immerse the curtain.\"", "Among the masters of the esoteric truth as well, it is found in the Zohar, Bereshit, on \"For in yet seven days\" [Gen 7:4]: \"R. Hiyya and R. Judah paced three hundred paces along one bone of the people of the Flood,\"", "comparable to which—without hyperbole—the chief of the Christian sages wrote in his City [Augustine, De civitate Dei], book 15, chapter 9, concerning the great bodily size of the giants: that he saw a human tooth which, if cut to the size of our teeth, would divide into a hundred teeth.", "Again there in the Zohar, Toledot Yitzhak, on the verse \"Behold, I have made him lord\" [Gen 27:37]: \"R. Simeon would state three hundred decided laws in the mystery of supernal wisdom on the verse 'and his wife's name was Mehetabel' [Gen 36:39],\" and many like these.", "All this is close to what Rashi wrote in chapter Kol Kitvei, in the name of Rabbenu ha-Levi, concerning that pearl which Yosef Mokir Shabbei sold for thirteen upper chambers [full of gold], etc.: that it is mere hyperbole, meaning an enormous fortune;", "and likewise everywhere, such as \"thirteen camels of doubtful terefot,\" and likewise \"thirteen butchers\" above;", "and explicitly concerning that [passage] in Tamid, chapter 2: \"At times there were three hundred kor of ashes in the middle of the altar\"—\"Rava said: hyperbole.\"", "Thus from all these it is revealed that the difficulty we raised from the aforementioned contradiction is truly resolved.", "As to the sum of high priests mentioned, know that Josephus, in the last chapter of his last book [of the Antiquities] for the Romans, wrote", "that from Aaron the priest until the end of the high priests of the Second Temple there were eighty-three high priests: thirteen from Aaron until Solomon's building, eighteen in the First Temple, and fifty-two in the Second Temple,", "as you will find in that chapter, which, with God's help, I shall copy in the fourth Essay, chapter 53.", "And although his total reckoning differs from the version of the Babylonian and the Yerushalmi above,", "I have thought it worthwhile to mention it for a reason I shall make known to you. It is that in the first chapter of Yoma, on the [statement] that eighteen high priests served in the First Temple, you will find in the Tosafot that Rabbenu Tam, because of a difficulty he raised, emended [it] to eight,", "and Ri rejected his words too and corrected [it] to twelve. But the words of both are rejected together, twice over, for the Yerushalmi too, in the first chapter of Yoma mentioned, reads eighteen, as follows:", "\"In the First [Temple], in which there served father, son, and grandson, eighteen high priests served.\"", "Such too is the reading of Vayikra Rabbah 21, which, as you know from Rashi's words, the Rabbot are aggadah of the Land of Israel; and so you will find in Sifrei at the end of Parashat Balak—and in accurate versions it is the beginning of Parashat Pinhas—as follows:", "\"'Therefore say' etc. [Num 25:12]: This teaches that in the First Building eighteen priest-prophets arose from him,", "but in the Last Building eighty prophet-priests arose from him, and because they would sell it for money their years began to be shortened.\" End of quote.", "For such is the correct reading according to what I saw in two very ancient manuscript copies of Sifrei.", "So too in Sifrei Zuta—which the author of the Arukh, s.v. tag, called Midrash Panim [Sheni], and which Rashi, of blessed memory, in his commentary on the Torah, Parashat Shemini, calls the Baraita of Panim Sheni—you will find as follows: ⚠", "\"In the First Temple eighteen high priests arose from him, and in the Second Temple eighty high priests, since they made it their practice to sell it for money,\" etc.", "Also the aforementioned Josephus, who was a priest and versed in the affairs of his city, wrote eighteen in the First Temple, as we mentioned.", "Let Rabbenu Tam and Ri, then, go and gather for themselves another resolution of their difficulty,", "for we have seen one among the external writers, namely Josephus for the Romans, and we have heard the voice of four from the earliest of our ancients' works—Yerushalmi, Bavli, Sifrei, and the Rabbot as mentioned—all of whom said eighteen high priests;", "and it is not right that we disqualify five valid witnesses on the strength of reasoning.", "Let it not be hidden from the reader that in the Tosafot to Zevahim, chapter Tevul Yom, this statement is found:", "\"We find in Chronicles that there were high priests only from Phinehas; and in Sifrei it is derived from 'My covenant of peace' [Num 25:12] that eight high priests arose from him in the First Temple and three hundred in the Second Temple, and all of them are counted in Sifrei.\"", "End of quote. But in the Piskei Tosafot derived from that passage you will find eighteen high priests;", "and your eyes, which look to faithfulness, will see in every version of Sifrei, both the Great and the Zuta, that they are not counted thus.", "Therefore it seems that one does not learn from that passage, whose reading is corrupt.", "And if in saying \"three hundred high priests in the Second Temple\" they meant literally three hundred,", "they must resolve for themselves the difficulty of the contradiction we raised. Also, have no doubt that the entire passage found in the printed commentary to Chronicles attributed to Rashi, on the verse \"he is Azariah who served as priest in the house that Solomon built\" [1 Chr 5:36], which rejects the reading eighteen and the reading eight and says that the correct [figure] is twelve,", "is not from Rashi, of blessed memory; for if so, he would have touched on it in his commentary to the first chapter of Yoma, and Rabbenu Tam and Ri would in some way have mentioned it in their words cited;", "and anyone who knows the character of his language will readily judge that that language is not of his usual kind,", "but necessarily some scholar wise in his own eyes added it there after seeing Ri's aforementioned emendation.", "And my soul rejoices in the Lord, for after I had written these words of mine from my own reasoning,", "I labored and found, in the possession of the honorable R. Moses, may he live long, a resident of Mantua, Rashi's commentary on the entire Scripture, gilded and very beautifully written in the year [5]068, that is, the 68th [year] of the sixth millennium, ⚠", "and behold, in Chronicles there is nothing whatever of that printed version,", "for in its place it is written as follows: \"'Azariah who served as priest in the house' etc.:", "Is it possible that he alone served as priest and no other? And if you say that he began to be priest in the house of the Lord—was not Zadok priest?", "And if you say that [Zadok] died and they gave him the priesthood—was there not Ahimaaz his son, who ought to have been priest?", "For so I say everywhere, that they would install in place of a priest who died only his son, and Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok.", "Rather, thus it is explained in the Yerushalmi: whoever gives himself over for the sanctification of the Lord or for the service of the Temple, [the matter] is called by his name;", "and this one gave himself over for the purity of the Temple, as is written below concerning the deed of King Uzziah: 'But when he was strong his heart was lifted up' etc., 'and he trespassed against his God' etc., 'and Azariah the priest went in after him' etc. [2 Chr 26:16-17];", "and since he gave himself over for the Temple, for so he said to the king, the priesthood is called by his name.\"", "End of quote. Then I said: Rejoice, my innermost being, rejoice! The sign has come that indeed my words were not false, which I wrote in the previous chapter about the signs of forgers of works;", "and the understanding man knows and bears witness what confusion a deceitful tongue gives and adds to the fair soul whose resting place is truth and righteousness."], "notes": [{"seg": 38, "he": "בעל ספר נופת צופים", "note": "Nofet Tzufim is by Judah Messer Leon; the gate/chapter reference is kept as given."}, {"seg": 55, "he": "פיקיי\"נו ... ראש חכמיהם", "note": "Identified as Marsilio Ficino's commentary on Plato's Symposium; 'their chief sage' is probably Augustine or Thomas Aquinas — uncertain."}, {"seg": 63, "he": "חזקיה בן גוריון", "note": "The Talmud reads Hananiah ben Hezekiah ben Garon; the text's form is kept. The three hundred jugs of oil were brought up for him (to light the room)."}, {"seg": 87, "he": "ערך טג ... מדרש פנים [שני]", "note": "Arukh entry and bracketed word as printed; identification of 'Panim Sheni' with Sifrei Zuta follows the author."}, {"seg": 104, "he": "שנת חס\"ר היינו ע\"ב לאלף הששי", "note": "חס\"ר = 268, i.e. 5268 (1508 CE), but the author's gloss reads ע\"ב (72); the gloss may be corrupt (perhaps for ס\"ח = 68).
